relevance_note: Case report of two brothers with LCAT deficiency and their carrier parents: "the proband was compound heterozygous for two novel LCAT variants".
method_note: Built by hand-entered Python script in scratch; every span located in the paper (spaces in quotes matched to the paper's non-breaking spaces and copied exactly). Labels: the paper gives no own labels ('Proband', 'Brother', 'Father', 'Mother' are role/relation words used as Table 2 column headers), so the proband is 'Table 2 column 1' (patients-as-columns rule) and relatives follow rule 2. Table 2 column headers: Proband, Brother, Father, Mother. Proband's age: 30 at admission; later course (hemodialysis 4 years later) has no stated age. Age 19 is the age at the earlier diagnosis of membranous nephropathy (later re-evaluated as LCAT deficiency), recorded only as onset of that feature, not as disease onset or diagnosis age. Contradictions/discrepancies: proband HDL 0.42 (Table 1, admission) vs 0.23 (Table 2) and TG 16.58 vs 7.36, total cholesterol 8.3 vs 4.70 (different visits per text); brother HDL 0.24 mmol/L in text vs 0.22 in Table 2 and triglycerides 4.28 mmol/l in text vs 1.85 in Table 2; brother 'age 27' vs '4-year younger' than a 30-year-old proband; Unesterified/total cholesterol reference value printed as '0.25' while values are in %. Brother's variants: the paper says only that 'the brothers are carriers of the same genetic variants'; zygosity and inheritance left not reported for him (D-29), parental carrier statements quoted. Transcript NM_000229 is stated once in Methods for the sequencing and applied to all rows. Father: Table 2 triglycerides 2.7 (ref <1.71) but text says no other signs of the disease; hypertriglyceridemia left not reported for him. Mother: HDL 0.91 (ref >1) yet called healthy; nothing recorded beyond 'healthy'. Brother 'red blood cell count within the lower normal range' recorded as low RBC count excluded; checklist anemia left not reported (RBC count, not hemoglobin). Brother 'preserved kidney function' excludes impaired function but not the composite 'chronic kidney disease or renal failure'. Brother reduced cholesteryl ester fraction left not reported (only the Table 2 ratio with an inconsistent reference). Hematuria for the proband based on 3–7 erythrocytes in urine sediment above the 0–2 reference. Table 1 lab values with reference ranges used for out-of-range features.
